label: def:information-bandwidth
title: Information bandwidth per Planck time
html:
Definition. The information bandwidth per Planck time quantifies the total information transferred across the causal boundary in one Planck step. It is the product of the speed of light c_q (speed of light) (fibres correlated per tick) and the operational entropy per fibre (operational entropy):

  \mathfrak{B}(q)
  = c_q \cdot n_R(q) \cdot \eta_q
  = \frac{\eta_q}{\hbar_q \cdot (q-1)}
  = \frac{\eta_q}{q^{-1}(q-1)^2}
  = \frac{q \cdot \eta_q}{(q-1)^2}.

At q = q_0, the bandwidth \mathfrak{B} = q\eta_q/(q-1)^2 \approx 82 q-bits per Planck time. This functions as the Bremermann-analog bit budget of the substrate. It dictates the maximum number of distinguishable q-bits that a single Planck step can carry across the light-cone boundary.
